theARBITRATIONOFTHE622VS579DISAGREEMENT.theQUESTION: FIX166 publishes addedGlyphsReadFromOutputBytes 622 canonical and 1,251 boundary. VF58 measured 579 and 1,170. FIX166 says the gap is definitional: 'a show-text glyph count inside the flattened widget appearance streams' against 'a per-page character-multiset difference against the pinned source pages using pdftotext'.
theARBITRATIONOFTHE622VS579DISAGREEMENT.theANSWER: IT IS SETTLEABLE FROM THE BYTES, AND FIX166'S EXPLANATION OF THE GAP IS WRONG. This lane implemented exactly the method FIX166 describes -- decompress each flattened widget Form XObject, decode every Tj/TJ operand, count glyphs -- and read 579 canonical and 1,170 boundary, which are VF58's numbers to the unit. Counting the SAME operands from the SAME streams with whitespace INCLUDED gives 622 and 1,251, which are FIX166's numbers to the unit. The two figures are not two methods. They are one method with and without the space character: 622 - 579 = 43 spaces on the canonical and 1,251 - 1,170 = 81 on the boundary.
theARBITRATIONOFTHE622VS579DISAGREEMENT.theMECHANISM_READFROMTHECODEANDTHEBYTES: The builder's reader at scripts/build-census-v1-il-seal-3yr-set.mjs strips whitespace with `text.replace(/\s/g, "").length / (operand.startsWith("<") ? 2 : 1)`. pdf-lib writes every one of these operands as a HEX string, so `text` is the hex DIGITS, and the strip removes whitespace from the hexadecimal, where there is none -- the space byte is the two hex characters '2' and '0'. Read out of the delivered canonical: <4A6F7264616E204176657279205265796573> is 'Jordan Avery Reyes', 36 hex digits, counted as 18 where the non-whitespace count is 16. The whitespace-stripping is applied to the encoding instead of to the decoded text.
theARBITRATIONOFTHE622VS579DISAGREEMENT.soWHICHISRIGHT: 622 is a TRUE reading of the delivered bytes: 622 characters really are shown by those 44 appearances. It is not a fabrication and it is not a literal, which is what the repair was for. But it is the whitespace-INCLUSIVE count published under a bare name, two keys above a definition string in the same JSON object that defines the companion counter in terms of 'at least one non-whitespace glyph'. A lane reading that block would reasonably take 622 for a non-whitespace figure. VF58's 579 is the non-whitespace count and it is correct; that VF58 reached it from pdftotext page text and this lane reached it from the appearance streams is corroboration, not conflict.
theARBITRATIONOFTHE622VS579DISAGREEMENT.theSECONDORDERPOINT: The same defect sits latent in flattenedWidgetAppearancesReadFromOutputBytes 44. Its published definition says an appearance counts when it draws 'at least one non-whitespace glyph', and the code that produced it cannot exclude whitespace from a hex operand. On THESE bytes it makes no difference -- this lane counted 44 inked appearances under the strict non-whitespace rule too -- but the published definition is not the implemented rule, and an appearance that drew only a space would be counted as inked.
theARBITRATIONOFTHE622VS579DISAGREEMENT.whatFIX166CLAIMEDABOUTITSOWNCHECK: FIX166 states that 'an independent re-implementation of the same reading, written outside the builder, reproduced every figure the builders now publish'. This lane's independent re-implementation reproduces 443 and 44 but reads 579, not 622, unless whitespace is deliberately counted. Whatever FIX166 re-implemented shared the builder's treatment of whitespace.
theARBITRATIONOFTHE622VS579DISAGREEMENT.whatWOULDSETTLEITINTHERECORD: Publish the non-whitespace figure under addedGlyphsReadFromOutputBytes and keep 622 under a name that says so, or rename the field. This is a record change with no fixture byte moved, so no raster is disturbed. It is not this lane's to make.
